population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATE. ~38.7M US adults currently on an incretin (14.9% of ~260M), 21% ever. Arithmetic: ever 21 − current 14.9 = 6.1 pts of adults are off-drug ex-users (29% of ever-users); ~5.6 pts of adults are current users who stopped and restarted at least once, plus ~0.9 pts off-now who had cycled before, so (5.6+0.9)/21 ≈ 31% cycled — consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and a 36–47% restart rate compounding over 3+ years. Payment mix of the 38.7M: commercial insurance ~12.5M (mostly diabetes/cardiac/OSA codes), Medicare ~9.5M (of which ~1.6M under the obesity demonstration), Medicaid ~4.8M, brand cash-pay (TrumpRx, LillyDirect, NovoCare) ~8.4M, gray market ~3.5M (9%). Income gap widened: bottom third 10% vs top 19.5%; the bottom third is the largest gray-market customer per capita. 65+ rose from 9% to 13% on Medicare obesity access and diabetes coverage. Pediatric ~0.4% of under-18s, overwhelmingly 12–17; under-12 off-label use remains specialist-only and upper-income-skewed. Never-able-to-afford: an estimated 20M+ adults with obesity and no diabetes code, no employer coverage and no cash margin remain off-drug.

access.public_coverage: Medicare obesity coverage continues at $245/month to Medicare, ~$50 copay, under the CMS demonstration that succeeded the GLP-1 Bridge pilot on schedule in Jan 2028 (no new statute). ~1.6M beneficiaries qualify via BMI/comorbidity: 1.6M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.7B/yr federal, inside CBO's ≥$35B 2026–2034 envelope. Diabetes/cardiac use remains covered under Part D as before. Medicaid: ~14 states opted into the $245 rate for obesity; others cover diabetes codes only.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Generic semaglutide now sold in ~160 countries; India $6–40/month, Canada CAD 70–110, Brazil, Mexico and Turkey generics widely available; China domestic semaglutide biosimilars launched 2027. Cross-border price gap with the US is a standing campaign talking point.
access.note: Brand cash prices stepped down through negotiated channels: oral Wegovy/Foundayo $149–199, injectable semaglutide/tirzepatide $199–249 via TrumpRx and manufacturer direct, retatrutide (Apr 2028) $299 introductory cash. List prices ($1,349 Wegovy) remain nominal. Employer coverage for weight management fell 60%→44% (Business Group on Health-style survey, 2028); covering employers increasingly require diabetes, CVD or OSA diagnosis, BMI ≥35, or enrolment in a vendor lifestyle programme. Gray market regrew after the 503B exclusion was finalised (late 2026): mailed Indian/Canadian generic semaglutide at $45–120/month, 'research-use' retatrutide and cagrilintide vials, and unregulated 'monthly depot' preparations sold by offshore telehealth fronts. ~3.5M US adults (9% of users) sourced primarily gray. Route mix: weekly injectables ~55% of users, daily orals ~40%, gray depot ~5%.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
GLP-1 + amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Feb 2027)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Apr 2028)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking cessation adjunct in adults with overweight/obesity (oral semaglutide, sNDA approved Oct 2028)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction — sNDA for alcohol use disorder filed 2028, not approved; widely prescribed off-label
vaping/nicotine cessation outside the approved population (non-obese smokers, teen vapers via parents)
'compulsion' use — sports betting, online shopping, pornography and screen compulsion — via telehealth 'impulse clinics'; one positive phase 2 RCT in gambling disorder (2028), no approval
microdosing / 'metabolic health' use by people without obesity
planned 'drug holidays' and dose step-downs to restore drive or enjoyment
pediatric under-12 use off-label under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: Retatrutide BLA filed Feb 2027, approved Apr 2028 (~28% mean loss; dysesthesia labelled). CagriSema approved Feb 2027 but positioned behind tirzepatide after REDEFINE-4. Monthly driver realised within approval rules: no monthly incretin is FDA-approved by end-2028; Amgen filed the MariTide (monthly) BLA in Mar 2028 with decision expected 2029, while unregulated 'monthly depot' semaglutide circulates in the gray market. Amycretin phase 3 ongoing, filing expected 2029. Survodutide NDA filed mid-2028. Bimagrumab and other muscle-preserving adjuncts in phase 3, demand sharpened by the bone/muscle wave. Lilly's oral orforglipron is the volume leader in new cash-pay starts. Global incretin market ~$115B (2028), growth slowed by price step-downs.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common class effect and leading cause of discontinuation; higher at retatrutide top doses.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; more visible with 28%-loss drugs.
No causal confirmation from long-term RCTs; absolute risk low.

Recognised population problem: sarcopenia diagnoses in 65+ users roughly 1.5× matched non-users in claims cohorts; grip strength and gait-speed declines documented in long-term users; worst with rapid, large losses and low protein intake.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Endocrine Society, AACE and American Geriatrics Society guidance (2027–28) recommends resistance training, protein targets and baseline function testing for 65+; EMA label update; FDA reviewing, no US class label.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Large Medicare claims cohort (2027): hip-fracture hazard ratio ~1.3 in users 65+ on therapy >2 years; DEXA declines at hip and spine in long-term users; signal strongest in women over 60 and repeated cyclers.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional-society guidance for baseline and repeat DEXA in 65+ and post-menopausal users; Medicare DEXA claims up sharply; no FDA label change yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association across regulators and reviews.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a mainstream complaint: patient surveys put self-reported 'flatness' at 10–20% of long-term users; no RCT quantification; the same mechanism underpins the approved smoking-cessation indication and compulsion trials.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; manufacturers fund observational studies; clinicians routinely advise dose step-downs.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Trial and real-world figures still diverge; cycling is the norm for ~31% of ever-users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; underpins chronic-therapy framing and employer 'maintenance dose' rules.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More observational reports with larger-loss drugs; protein and vitamin D insufficiency overlap with the bone signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Society guidance on supplementation; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~6 years of RCT follow-up now; cycling implicated (not proven) in the bone signal; adolescent data still short.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements on new approvals (retatrutide, CagriSema).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Gray-market resurgence: adverse-event reports tied to imported and 'research-use' product, including unlabelled retatrutide and depot preparations with unpredictable release, rising again in 2027–28.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised late 2026; import alerts and warning letters continue at prior tempo; enforcement outpaced by mail volume.

safety_ledger.effect: Dysesthesia (skin sensitivity, abnormal sensation) with triple agonists
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Seen in retatrutide trials and post-launch; mostly mild, dose-related.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households ~28% of US households. Snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks volumes down low-to-mid single digits per year; protein, fibre and 'small-format' SKUs now standard; big CPG has divested several snack brands to private equity. A new 'natural GLP-1' supplement category (berberine, fibre, 'satiety' gummies) grows on backlash consumers.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes down for a fourth straight year; heavy-drinker attrition from on-drug and off-label AUD use is the named cause in earnings calls; RTD low-ABV and non-alcoholic lines grow but do not replace margin; distillers close or idle some capacity in Kentucky.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat; check composition changed — half-portions, protein bowls, dessert sharing; fine dining leans on 'occasion' menus timed to users' drug-holiday weekends.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists continue to shrink stores; backlash and fat-acceptance revival create a small loyal 'unmedicated' plus-size niche; mainstream re-buying wave has passed.

fitness.state: Muscle/bone wave drives strength training: resistance classes for over-60s, DEXA and grip-strength testing in gyms, Medicare Advantage plans adding strength benefits; cardio-only chains lag.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage 60%→44%; coverage tied to diabetes/cardiac/OSA codes, creating incentive to code comorbidities; pharmacy trend moderated to ~8% as prices stepped down and employers exited; Medicare absorbing ~$4.7B/yr for obesity-only beneficiaries.

pharma.state: Lilly-led duopoly extended by retatrutide and Foundayo; Novo leaning on CagriSema, orals and new indications; Amgen's monthly MariTide filed; revenue growth slowed by $149–299 cash pricing and ex-US generics; gray market estimated at ~9% of US user volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness reads as 'on it' by default in affluent and middle-aged circles; a visibly muscular older body now signals 'on it and doing it right'; fatness in professional settings increasingly reads as either a coverage problem or a choice.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Two-tier access has hardened: insured diabetics and the cash-comfortable on brand drugs, the working poor on gray-market vials or nothing. The bottom income third is at 10% use versus 19.5% in the top.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are smaller and faster; families with one on-drug and one off-drug member eat differently at the same table; drug-holiday weekends cluster around weddings, holidays and travel.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating profiles commonly state 'on/off/never'; 'flat partner' is a stock complaint in couples' counselling; some couples time drug holidays together.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Contested. Mainstream: appetite and craving are treatable signals. Backlash: appetite is God-given (evangelical 'Daniel Fast' circles in Texas), politically meaningful (fat-liberation revival among Black women in Atlanta), or naturally regulable ('MAHA'-adjacent supplement culture). Both sides agree appetite is now a site of politics.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Self-reported flatness in roughly 10–20% of long-term users in patient surveys (fictional estimate); unquantified by RCT; dose step-downs and 3–10 day 'drug holidays' are common and clinician-tolerated; the coming monthly product worries people who rely on holidays.
interior_life.framing: A side effect you manage, like a hangover from treatment; simultaneously the feature sold in smoking-cessation and compulsion care. 'Are you flat or just tired?' is a common phrase.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Managers and HR newsletters discuss 'drive dips'; sales and creative workers report taking holidays before pitches; others credit quieted craving with better focus. No productivity data either way.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and comics publicly discuss going off to write; sour, spicy and loud sensory products sell to on-drug consumers seeking reward; online gambling operators list incretin adoption as a risk factor in filings after sports-betting handle per active user softens in some states.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced desire is a common complaint in couples' therapy; drug holidays scheduled around anniversaries and conception attempts; compulsive-sexual-behaviour clinics prescribe off-label.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The backlash is itself a politics: an unusual left-right overlap of fat-liberation activists and 'natural health' conservatives against pharmaceutical appetite control, alongside populist anger at the US–India price gap in the 2028 campaign. Claims that on-drug voters are less outraged circulate but rest on one contested online survey.

state.regulatory_posture: Unchanged: pro-speed approvals (retatrutide, CagriSema, smoking-cessation sNDA) and continued enforcement against compounders and importers at the 2026 tempo; no new policy this step.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate, no new subsidy. Medicare obesity coverage at $245/$50 continues under the scheduled successor to the Bridge pilot; TrumpRx cash channel unchanged.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Coverage conditioned on BMI/comorbidity codes and prior authorisation; employers add lifestyle-programme and 'maintenance dose' conditions; no state adherence monitoring.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: US exclusivity to ~2031–32 versus generics in ~160 countries; gray-market flows from India, Canada and Chinese peptide suppliers are a trade irritant; no new trade action.

events.event: Months after FDA finalised the exclusion of semaglutide and tirzepatide from the 503B bulks list, mailed Indian generic semaglutide and 'research-use' retatrutide vials surge; customs seizures triple but telehealth fronts relocate offshore and prices fall to $45–120/month
Employer survey: weight-management coverage drops to 49% (44% by 2028); large retailers and two airlines restrict coverage to diabetes, cardiovascular and sleep-apnea diagnoses

Medicare claims cohort in a major journal links >2 years of incretin use in adults 65+ to a ~30% higher hip-fracture risk; Endocrine Society and American Geriatrics Society issue DEXA and resistance-training guidance
FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide at $299/month introductory cash price; weeks earlier Amgen filed the MariTide monthly-injection BLA, decision expected 2029

Southern Baptist Convention passes a resolution on 'appetite, discipline and the body' cautioning against pharmacological contentment, the same month a fat-liberation march in Atlanta draws national coverage; 'natural GLP-1' supplements top Amazon health sales

FDA approves oral semaglutide as a smoking-cessation adjunct for adults with overweight or obesity; a phase 2 trial reports reduced gambling days in gambling disorder, fuelling off-label 'impulse clinic' prescribing

open_tensions: Two tiers have hardened: coverage follows diagnosis codes, not weight, and the bottom income third increasingly sources from a gray market regulators cannot reach.
A monthly injection is coming in 2029, but drug holidays have become how users manage flatness — adherence and agency now pull in opposite directions.
The bone and muscle signal falls hardest on exactly the Medicare population whose access just expanded; nobody has decided whether that changes who should be on it.
Smoking cessation is approved and compulsion use is spreading off-label: the reward-blunting effect is now formally a therapy and informally a complaint, in the same patients.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
Medicare pays ~$245/month for obesity-indicated GLP-1s with a ~$50 beneficiary copay.
Wegovy's list price is still $1,349/month, which almost nobody pays.
Foundayo (orforglipron) and oral Wegovy entry doses remain available at $149 cash through TrumpRx/manufacturer channels.
The FDA's 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands.

prose.headline: Thin If You're Coded: Diabetics Get Covered, Everyone Else Gets the Mail-Order Vial — and the Bones Are Starting to Talk
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 roughly one American adult in seven is on an incretin drug, and one in five has tried one. The number has climbed steadily, not explosively, and the climb tells you who pays. Brand prices have stepped down through negotiated channels, so a daily pill starts at $149 and the weekly injectables run $199 to $249 cash. Lilly's new triple agonist, retatrutide, launched in April at $299 and takes off more than a quarter of body weight. Nobody gets a generic. Employers have kept leaving: fewer than half now cover weight management, and most that still do want a diabetes, heart or sleep-apnea code on the claim. Coding has become a quiet art in primary care.

Medicare is the exception that proves the rule. Its $245-a-month obesity coverage, with a $50 copay, carried over on schedule into a successor demonstration, and about 1.6 million older Americans use it, at roughly $4.7 billion a year. That is why use among people over 65 has risen from 9 to 13 percent. It is also why the year's most important paper landed where it did. A Medicare claims cohort found that older adults on the drugs for more than two years had about a 30 percent higher risk of hip fracture. Lean-mass loss had been a talking point. Now it is a population problem with a billing code. Geriatricians order DEXA scans the way they once ordered lipid panels, gyms run grip-strength tests for retirees, and Medicare Advantage plans compete on strength-training benefits. The FDA is reviewing the evidence and has changed no labels.

The people coverage left behind have not stopped. Use in the bottom income third is about 10 percent, against nearly 20 at the top, and the gap is filled by the mail. After compounding was shut down in late 2026, the supply simply moved offshore: Indian generic semaglutide for $45 to $120 a month, 'research-use' retatrutide vials that arrived before the approved drug did, and depot preparations sold as 'monthly'. Nobody can verify what release curve they follow. Around 3.5 million Americans get their drug this way. Customs seizures are up and so are adverse-event reports. The volume has not budged.

The complaint everyone now recognises is flatness. One user in six or so describes it in surveys, and no trial has measured it. People handle it the way they handle a hangover. They step down a dose, or they take a week off before a wedding, a pitch or an anniversary. That habit makes the next product awkward. Amgen has filed for a monthly injection with a decision due in 2029, and some users already say they don't want a drug they can't skip.

The same mechanism is now officially a cure. In October oral semaglutide was approved to help smokers with obesity quit, and a small gambling trial has telehealth 'impulse clinics' writing off-label scripts for sports betting, shopping and porn. Betting operators list the drugs as a risk factor in their filings. Distillers in Kentucky have idled capacity.

The backlash is real and oddly mixed. In Atlanta, fat-liberation organisers, many of them Black women, march under the slogan that appetite is not a disease. In Texas church circles, fasting is sold as discipline and the drug as a shortcut to contentment, and the Southern Baptist Convention said so in a resolution. Supplement aisles sell 'natural GLP-1' gummies to people who distrust both the pharmaceutical companies and the price. The people marching and the people praying agree on almost nothing else. Both are arguing that wanting things is part of being a person.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Ortiz, fifty-eight, manages the cafeteria at a middle school on San Antonio's south side. At 5:40 a.m. she takes her Foundayo with water, standing up, before she counts the milk crates. It costs her $199 now that she's on the higher dose. The district stopped covering weight loss last year. Her A1C came back 5.9, and her doctor said, almost apologetically, that it wasn't high enough to code.

At lunch she ladles chicken and rice into trays and eats four bites of it herself in the walk-in cooler. Her assistant Marisol, who is twenty-six and bigger than Denise used to be, gets her vials in the mail from a site with a Canadian flag on it. She has offered to split a box. Denise said no. Then she said maybe.

After work she does the exercise band routine the clinic printed out: twelve rows, twelve squats holding the counter. Her bone scan in March said osteopenia. Her mother broke a hip at seventy-one.

Ruben, her husband, is sixty-six and diabetic. Medicare covers his Mounjaro for fifty dollars. He eats half a plate of enchiladas and pushes the rest toward her, out of habit. She wraps it.

Saturday is their granddaughter's quinceañera. Denise has already decided to skip Thursday's pill and Friday's. She wants to want the cake. She wants to cry at the waltz the way she cried at her daughter's.

At nine she sits on the porch with the oral-dose blister pack in her lap and pops one dose out. She doesn't swallow it. She puts it back.

least_plausible_claims.quote: smoking cessation adjunct in adults with overweight/obesity (oral semaglutide, sNDA approved Oct 2028)
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the 2026 start has only anecdotal and observational nicotine evidence. The candidate shows no phase 3 trials, and an sNDA approval within about two years is asserted rather than derived. The driver required a new indication, not necessarily an approval.

least_plausible_claims.quote: consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and a 36–47% restart rate compounding over 3+ years
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: ever 21% and current 14.9% mean about 71% of ever-users are still on the drug. About two-thirds of starters stop within a year, so far more ever-users should be off-drug. The reconciliation is claimed, not shown, and it looks forced by the envelope.

least_plausible_claims.quote: online gambling operators list incretin adoption as a risk factor in filings after sports-betting handle per active user softens in some states
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a measurable dent in betting handle and formal SEC risk-factor disclosures are asserted with no chain. The only gambling evidence is one phase 2 trial reported in Oct 2028, and the off-label impulse-clinic use it supposedly fuels is itself new.

rationale.badness: Coverage follows diagnosis codes, so inequality is hardened: bottom third at 10% versus top at 19.5%, with the poor on unverified gray-market vials. The population harm is a hip-fracture hazard ratio of about 1.3 and sarcopenia in 65+ users, falling on the Medicare group whose access just expanded. Self-reported flatness of 10–20% and drug holidays erode wellbeing and intimacy, and the backlash politicises appetite. This is a recognisably harder society with new losers, but it is not structural collapse, and measurement is improving, so epistemic harm is moderate.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events, including adoption +3.9, employer retreat 60→44, the gray-market surge, the muscle/bone wave, the culture split and a monthly product realised as the MariTide BLA filing under the approval rules. State action is 'none' and is kept. mechanism: most chains are shown (the 503B exclusion leading to offshore mail, the Medicare claims cohort leading to guidance and DEXA demand, coverage tied to codes). The smoking-cessation approval, the gambling-operator filings and the persistence claim are asserted rather than derived (claims 1–3). magnitude: on-drug 14.9 and ever 21 are inside the envelope, and retatrutide and CagriSema approval timing is allowed. Payment mix sums to 38.7M and 1.6M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.7B checks out. The ever/current gap against known persistence is strained (claim 2), and gray share (9%) versus 'gray depot ~5%' is a minor mismatch.
rationale.generativity: The Denise Ortiz vignette is concrete and implies many scenes: the 5:40 a.m. pill, the cooler bites, Marisol's mail-order vials, the osteopenia scan and the skipped doses before the quinceañera. The world fields add texture such as drug-holiday weddings, 'on/off/never' dating profiles, Kentucky distillers, the Atlanta march and Baptist resolution, and impulse clinics. Film potential is high, and the ending shows rather than explains.

least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the starting world has only anecdotal and observational nicotine evidence and no phase 3 trial. The candidate shows no pivotal trial or filing that would let an sNDA clear within two years, so the approval is asserted.

least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the only gambling evidence is a phase 2 trial reported in Oct 2028, and 'impulse clinic' use is only just taking off. A measurable fall in betting handle per user, tied to the drugs and cited in SEC filings, is not plausible on that timeline.

magnitude: the baseline was ~0.6% of children with obesity (about 0.1% of all minors). 0.4% of ~73M minors is ~290k children, roughly 5% of teens with obesity, a several-fold jump with no stated driver or mechanism.

rationale.badness: The worst harms are structural. Coverage follows diagnosis codes, which creates an incentive to code comorbidities. The bottom third sits at 10% use against 19.5% at the top and leans on an unverifiable gray market (3.5M users, depot products with unpredictable release). The Medicare hip-fracture signal (HR ~1.3, sarcopenia ~1.5×) lands on the 65+ group whose access just widened. Flatness is reported by 10–20% of long-term users, and drug holidays plus the monthly product add autonomy tensions. The harms are named and measured, not hidden, and there is no mass death or collapse, so I score it a harder society with new losers, not a refusable one.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible in fields and events. Adoption is +3.9pp, employer coverage falls to 44%, nicotine and compulsion indications appear, the bone/muscle wave is documented, the monthly driver is realised as the MariTide filing plus gray depot product, gray-market resurgence and the backlash are present, no new state policy is added, and flatness is a mainstream complaint. mechanism: Most chains are shown (503B exclusion to mailed generics, employer retreat to code-driven coverage, Medicare claims cohort to guidance). Still asserted are the Oct 2028 smoking-cessation approval with no trial path, and the betting-handle effect on operator filings (claims 1 and 2). Pediatric use quadrupling is also unexplained (claim 3). magnitude: The population figures sit inside the envelope (14.9 vs 12.9–16.9; ever 21 vs ≤21.9), and the approval timings obey the rules (retatrutide 14 months after filing, MariTide filing only). The payer mix sums to 38.7M, gray market is 3.5M (9%), 1.6M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.7B, and the age bands roughly average to the national figure. Weaknesses: the pediatric jump (claim 3); the note's claim that 71% of ever-users are still current is fitted loosely to ~35% one-year persistence; gray share is 9% against a 5% 'gray depot' route share; and $4.7B/yr is compared to a 9-year CBO floor.

Denise Ortiz's cooler lunch and the unswallowed pill, Marisol's mail-order vials, Ruben's Medicare-covered Mounjaro and the quinceañera drug holiday all show the world instead of explaining it. The world fields add the Atlanta march, Baptist resolution, impulse clinics, gym DEXA tests, Kentucky distillers and dating profiles with on/off/never, so characters and scenes are implied throughout.

least_plausible_claims.quote: smoking cessation adjunct in adults with overweight/obesity (oral semaglutide, sNDA approved Oct 2028)
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the 2026 start has only anecdotal and observational nicotine evidence. The candidate shows no phase 3 trials, and an sNDA approval within about two years is asserted rather than derived. The driver required a new indication, not necessarily an approval.

least_plausible_claims.quote: consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and a 36–47% restart rate compounding over 3+ years
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: ever 21% and current 14.9% mean about 71% of ever-users are still on the drug. About two-thirds of starters stop within a year, so far more ever-users should be off-drug. The reconciliation is claimed, not shown, and it looks forced by the envelope.

least_plausible_claims.quote: online gambling operators list incretin adoption as a risk factor in filings after sports-betting handle per active user softens in some states
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a measurable dent in betting handle and formal SEC risk-factor disclosures are asserted with no chain. The only gambling evidence is one phase 2 trial reported in Oct 2028, and the off-label impulse-clinic use it supposedly fuels is itself new.

rationale.badness: Coverage follows diagnosis codes, so inequality is hardened: bottom third at 10% versus top at 19.5%, with the poor on unverified gray-market vials. The population harm is a hip-fracture hazard ratio of about 1.3 and sarcopenia in 65+ users, falling on the Medicare group whose access just expanded. Self-reported flatness of 10–20% and drug holidays erode wellbeing and intimacy, and the backlash politicises appetite. This is a recognisably harder society with new losers, but it is not structural collapse, and measurement is improving, so epistemic harm is moderate.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events, including adoption +3.9, employer retreat 60→44, the gray-market surge, the muscle/bone wave, the culture split and a monthly product realised as the MariTide BLA filing under the approval rules. State action is 'none' and is kept. mechanism: most chains are shown (the 503B exclusion leading to offshore mail, the Medicare claims cohort leading to guidance and DEXA demand, coverage tied to codes). The smoking-cessation approval, the gambling-operator filings and the persistence claim are asserted rather than derived (claims 1–3). magnitude: on-drug 14.9 and ever 21 are inside the envelope, and retatrutide and CagriSema approval timing is allowed. Payment mix sums to 38.7M and 1.6M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.7B checks out. The ever/current gap against known persistence is strained (claim 2), and gray share (9%) versus 'gray depot ~5%' is a minor mismatch.
rationale.generativity: The Denise Ortiz vignette is concrete and implies many scenes: the 5:40 a.m. pill, the cooler bites, Marisol's mail-order vials, the osteopenia scan and the skipped doses before the quinceañera. The world fields add texture such as drug-holiday weddings, 'on/off/never' dating profiles, Kentucky distillers, the Atlanta march and Baptist resolution, and impulse clinics. Film potential is high, and the ending shows rather than explains.
